exposure: Anti-incontinence surgery (transobturator tape surgery, other anti-incontinence surgeries, restorative surgeries)
outcome: Urinary incontinence (stress UI, urgency UI, occult UI, mixed UI)
cohort: The study included 56 women with overactive bladder symptoms and stress or urgency urinary incontinence, with or without prolapse, who were candidates for restorative and anti-incontinence surgery.
finding: Six months after anti-incontinence or reconstructive surgery, nocturia improved completely in all patients, urinary frequency improved partially or completely in 89% of patients, and various forms of urinary incontinence improved partially or completely in 95% of patients.
